currency.incremental_note: IMPLEMENTED (Step 5). Watermark = MAX(date) actually observed in rates (never a requested-but-unpublished date); next run requests {watermark+1}..{today} via date_range_url_template. Both the initial backfill and incremental loads use the range endpoint — plain 'url' (/latest) is kept here as documentation of the source's simplest endpoint but is not called by run() anymore. Verified live (Phase: FinPay source realignment): Frankfurter silently clips a requested range to the dates it actually has (e.g. weekends), rather than erroring or padding — confirmed by requesting 2026-09-17..2026-09-19 and receiving end_date=2026-09-18.

merchant_osm.incremental_note: IMPLEMENTED (Step 4). Same bbox/shop/amenity scope as the full query, restructured into Overpass QL's required set-then-filter grammar for `newer:` (a single-statement chained filter is not valid QL). Verified live: needs a >=60s Overpass QL timeout (25s -> HTTP 504) and the centralized User-Agent (absent -> HTTP 406). Uses `out meta;` to capture timestamp/version/changeset per element.
merchant_osm.user_agent_note: User-Agent is sourced from the centralized src/ingestion/settings.py, not from this file — verified live: a request without one returns HTTP 406.

iso_currency.note: AlphabeticCode repeats once per entity in the raw file (expected, not a defect) — Silver will dedupe to one row per currency.

card_issuer.note: ~374,788 rows / ~26MB, full dataset ingested per 2026-09-20 approval. ~48% of rows have a blank Issuer — expected, not a parse failure.

gleif.scope_note: LOCKED (Step 6E). Initial load: a deterministic 10,000-record (50-page at page[size]=200) portfolio-scoped extract from the GB + ACTIVE + ISSUED population (confirmed 95,078 total, verified live in Step 6B and cross-confirmed in Step 6D), ordered by sort=lei for reproducibility. This is NOT complete GB coverage and NOT a statistically representative sample. Incremental runs are NOT subject to this cap and paginate through the complete matching incremental result set.
gleif.sampling_limitation: sort=lei is deterministic (reproducible paging across runs) but NOT statistically representative: LEI codes encode the issuing Local Operating Unit (LOU) in their prefix, so ascending-LEI order clusters records by issuing LOU rather than by any business attribute — verified live in Step 6D (5 consecutive sorted records shared a common leading-character pattern). Must never be described as 'all UK entities', 'all GB entities', 'complete GB coverage', or 'representative statistical sampling'.
gleif.verification_note: Combined filters verified live in Step 6B (HTTP 200, total=95,078, page[size]=1). sort=lei verified live in Step 6D (HTTP 200, deterministic ascending order confirmed across 5 records, total cross-confirmed as 95,078 at page[size]=5 via lastPage=19,016).
gleif.observed_jurisdiction_values_note: OBSERVED (Step 6F real run, 10,000 records, run_20260921T054417Z): the GLEIF API request uses filter[entity.jurisdiction]=GB. In the real initial extraction, the API returned records whose entity.jurisdiction values included GB (9,949), GB-SCT (34), and GB-NIR (17). Therefore, downstream logic must not assume that the returned jurisdiction value is literally GB for every record.
